title: Reductant Injection Air Pump Control Circuit/Open
plain: The engine computer can't properly control the reductant injection air pump, which supplies air that helps atomize diesel exhaust fluid on some systems. It sees an open or broken circuit, often from wiring, a connector or the part itself.
symptoms: Check engine light on
DEF or emissions warning on the dash
A countdown to reduced speed may start if not repaired

causes.name: Blown fuse or bad relay feeding the circuit

checks: Inspect the air pump connector and wiring
Check for power at the connector and measure the part's resistance
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the reductant air pump.

title: Reductant Injection Air Pump Control Circuit Low
plain: The control circuit for the reductant injection air pump is reading low voltage. This part supplies air that helps atomize diesel exhaust fluid on some systems. A wire shorted to ground or a shorted part is the usual reason.
symptoms: Check engine light on
DEF or emissions warning on the dash
A countdown to reduced speed may start if not repaired
checks: Check the air pump wiring for rubbed-through insulation
Measure the air pump resistance and compare with spec
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the reductant air pump.

title: Reductant Injection Air Pump Control Circuit High
plain: The control circuit for the reductant injection air pump is reading high voltage. This part supplies air that helps atomize diesel exhaust fluid on some systems. A wire shorted to power, an open circuit or a failed part is the usual reason.
symptoms: Check engine light on
DEF or emissions warning on the dash
A countdown to reduced speed may start if not repaired

causes.name: Control wire shorted to a power source

checks: Check the air pump wiring for shorts to other wires
Measure the air pump resistance and compare with spec
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the reductant air pump.

title: Reductant Supply Control Circuit/Open

symptoms: Check engine light on
DEF or emissions warning on the dash
A countdown to reduced speed may start if not repaired

causes.name: Failed DEF supply pump or pump module
Blown fuse or bad relay feeding the circuit

checks: Inspect the DEF pump connector and wiring
Check for power at the connector and measure the part's resistance
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the DEF supply pump or pump module.

A countdown to reduced speed may start if not repaired

causes.name: Internally shorted DEF supply pump or pump module

checks: Check the DEF pump wiring for rubbed-through insulation
Measure the DEF pump resistance and compare with spec
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the DEF supply pump or pump module.

title: Reductant Supply Control Circuit High
plain: The control circuit for the reductant (DEF) supply pump is reading high voltage. This part pressurizes diesel exhaust fluid and sends it to the injector. A wire shorted to power, an open circuit or a failed part is the usual reason.

fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the DEF supply pump or pump module.

title: Fuel Level Sensor B Circuit
plain: The engine computer has found a problem in the circuit for the fuel level sensor B, which reads the fuel level in the second half of a saddle-shaped fuel tank (used on many all-wheel-drive cars and trucks). It usually points to wiring, a connector or the sensor itself.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Fuel gauge reads wrong or jumps around
Low fuel warning may come on at the wrong time

causes.name: Faulty fuel level sending unit B

checks: Inspect the fuel level sensor connector and wiring for damage or corrosion
Check the sensor power, ground and signal with a meter
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the fuel level sending unit B.

cost.job: Replace fuel level sending unit B

title: Fuel Level Sensor B Performance
plain: The fuel level sensor B is giving readings that don't make sense compared with what the computer expects. This sensor reads the fuel level in the second half of a saddle-shaped fuel tank (used on many all-wheel-drive cars and trucks). The sensor may be failing or the system it watches may have a real problem.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Fuel gauge reads wrong or jumps around
Low fuel warning may come on at the wrong time

causes.name: Failing or out-of-calibration fuel level sending unit B
Sticking float arm or worn sender track
High resistance in the wiring or connector

checks: Compare the fuel level sensor reading with related sensors in live data
Check wiring and connector for corrosion or looseness
fix: Confirm the system itself is working, then replace the fuel level sending unit B if its readings are off.

cost.job: Replace fuel level sending unit B

title: Fuel Level Sensor B Circuit Low
plain: The signal from the fuel level sensor B is lower than the computer expects. This sensor reads the fuel level in the second half of a saddle-shaped fuel tank (used on many all-wheel-drive cars and trucks). A wire shorted to ground or a failed sensor is the usual reason.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Fuel gauge reads wrong or jumps around
Low fuel warning may come on at the wrong time

causes.name: Signal or reference wire shorted to ground
Failed fuel level sending unit B

checks: Inspect the fuel level sensor wiring for rubbed-through or pinched spots
Unplug the sensor and see if the reading changes, which helps separate wiring from sensor
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the fuel level sending unit B.

cost.job: Replace fuel level sending unit B

title: Fuel Level Sensor B Circuit High
plain: The signal from the fuel level sensor B is higher than the computer expects. This sensor reads the fuel level in the second half of a saddle-shaped fuel tank (used on many all-wheel-drive cars and trucks). An open (broken) wire, a bad ground or a failed sensor is the usual reason.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Fuel gauge reads wrong or jumps around
Low fuel warning may come on at the wrong time

causes.name: Open or broken signal or ground wire
Failed fuel level sending unit B
Wire shorted to a power source

checks: Make sure the fuel level sensor connector is fully plugged in and clean
Check the sensor ground and signal wire for an open circuit
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the fuel level sending unit B.

cost.job: Replace fuel level sending unit B

title: Fuel Level Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
plain: The signal from the fuel level sensor B keeps dropping out or jumping around. This sensor reads the fuel level in the second half of a saddle-shaped fuel tank (used on many all-wheel-drive cars and trucks). A loose connection or a damaged wire is the usual reason.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Fuel gauge reads wrong or jumps around
Low fuel warning may come on at the wrong time

causes.name: Chafed wire that opens or shorts as the engine moves
Failing fuel level sending unit B

checks: Wiggle the harness and connector while watching live data for dropouts
Inspect the fuel level sensor wiring along its whole route
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the fuel level sending unit B.

cost.job: Replace fuel level sending unit B

title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Stuck Open
plain: The intake manifold tuning valve, which switches the path air takes through the intake to boost power at different speeds, appears stuck open.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Slightly weaker power at low or high engine speeds
Possible rattle from the intake

causes.name: Carbon buildup or broken valve linkage
Vacuum leak on a vacuum-operated valve

checks: Command the valve with a scan tool and watch it move
Check wiring, connector and any vacuum lines
fix: Replace the intake manifold tuning valve if it is stuck or broken.

title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Stuck Closed
plain: The intake manifold tuning valve, which switches the path air takes through the intake to boost power at different speeds, appears stuck closed.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Slightly weaker power at low or high engine speeds
Possible rattle from the intake

causes.name: Carbon buildup or broken valve linkage
Vacuum leak on a vacuum-operated valve

checks: Command the valve with a scan tool and watch it move
Check wiring, connector and any vacuum lines
fix: Replace the intake manifold tuning valve if it is stuck or broken.

title: Electronic Throttle Control System Performance - Ice Blockage
plain: The computer believes ice has formed in the throttle body and is keeping the throttle from moving normally. This tends to happen in freezing, wet weather.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced power or limp mode
Throttle may not respond normally in cold weather

causes.name: Ice in the throttle body from moisture in freezing weather
Blocked or leaking crankcase vent letting moisture into the intake

checks: Let the engine warm up fully and recheck
Inspect the intake and crankcase vent hoses for water or blockage
fix: Warm the vehicle to clear the ice and fix any source of water in the intake; replace the throttle body if it keeps sticking.

title: Manifold Absolute Pressure/Mass Air Flow - Throttle Position Correlation at Idle
plain: The computer compares how much air the engine is taking in (at idle) with how far the throttle is open, and the numbers don't agree. A vacuum leak or a bad airflow sensor is the usual cause.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Rough idle or stalling
Possible reduced power mode

causes.name: Dirty or faulty mass airflow (MAF) sensor

checks: Check for vacuum leaks and loose intake ducts
Compare MAF, MAP and throttle readings in live data
fix: Fix any air leak, then clean or replace the airflow or pressure sensor if readings are still off.

title: Manifold Absolute Pressure/Mass Air Flow - Throttle Position Correlation at Higher Load
plain: The computer compares how much air the engine is taking in (under heavier load) with how far the throttle is open, and the numbers don't agree. A vacuum leak or a bad airflow sensor is the usual cause.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Hesitation or loss of power when accelerating
Possible reduced power mode

causes.name: Dirty or faulty mass airflow (MAF) sensor

checks: Check for vacuum leaks and loose intake ducts
Compare MAF, MAP and throttle readings in live data
fix: Fix any air leak, then clean or replace the airflow or pressure sensor if readings are still off.

title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit

Slightly weaker power at some engine speeds

causes.name: Faulty intake manifold tuning valve (sensor is usually built in)

checks: Inspect the tuning valve connector and wiring for damage or corrosion
Check the sensor power, ground and signal with a meter
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the intake manifold tuning valve (sensor is usually built in).

title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1
plain: The exhaust gas temperature sensor (bank 1, sensor 1) is giving readings that don't make sense compared with what the computer expects. This sensor measures exhaust heat to protect the turbo, catalytic converter or particulate filter. The sensor may be failing or the system it watches may have a real problem.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Particulate filter cleaning may be blocked on diesels
Possible reduced power on some vehicles

causes.name: Failing or out-of-calibration exhaust gas temperature sensor
Exhaust leak or a real temperature problem in the exhaust
High resistance in the wiring or connector

checks: Compare the EGT sensor reading with related sensors in live data
Check wiring and connector for corrosion or looseness
fix: Confirm the system itself is working, then replace the exhaust gas temperature sensor if its readings are off.

title: "A" Camshaft Position Actuator Control Circuit Low Bank 1
plain: The control circuit for the camshaft timing control solenoid ("A" camshaft, bank 1) is reading low voltage. This part uses engine oil to adjust camshaft timing (variable valve timing). A wire shorted to ground or a shorted part is the usual reason.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Rough idle or stalling in some cases
Less power or poorer fuel economy
checks: Check the cam timing solenoid wiring for rubbed-through insulation
Measure the cam timing solenoid resistance and compare with spec
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the camshaft timing (VVT) solenoid.

title: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Lean Bank 1
plain: The oxygen sensor after the catalytic converter on bank 1 (the side of the engine with cylinder 1) shows the engine has been running too lean for the computer's fine-tuning to fix. This usually points to a problem before the converter, such as an exhaust or vacuum leak.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Usually no change in how the car drives
Possible drop in fuel economy

causes.name: Exhaust leak near the oxygen sensors
Low fuel pressure or clogged injectors

checks: Fix any other fuel trim, misfire or O2 sensor codes first
Check for exhaust leaks ahead of and around the O2 sensors
Compare upstream and downstream O2 sensor readings and fuel trims
fix: Find and repair the leak first; replace the downstream O2 sensor or catalytic converter only after testing.
drive: Usually drivable normally while you arrange a check. If the engine runs rough, misfires, hesitates or the check engine light starts flashing, cut back driving and get it checked promptly, since a lean condition can lead to misfires and damage.
test_first: Look for exhaust leaks near the oxygen sensors and intake vacuum leaks, check fuel trims and the rear oxygen sensor, and confirm catalyst health before replacing sensors or the converter.

title: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Rich Bank 1
plain: The oxygen sensor after the catalytic converter on bank 1 (the side of the engine with cylinder 1) shows the engine has been running too rich for the computer's fine-tuning to fix. This usually points to a problem before the converter, such as a leaking injector or high fuel pressure.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Usually no change in how the car drives
Possible drop in fuel economy
Possible rotten egg smell from the exhaust

causes.name: Faulty upstream or downstream oxygen sensor

checks: Fix any other fuel trim, misfire or O2 sensor codes first
Check for exhaust leaks ahead of and around the O2 sensors
Compare upstream and downstream O2 sensor readings and fuel trims
fix: Find and repair the rich running cause first; replace the downstream O2 sensor or catalytic converter only after testing.
drive: Usually drivable normally while you arrange a check. If you smell strong rotten eggs or fuel, see black smoke, or the light starts flashing, get it checked soon, because running rich can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter.
test_first: Check fuel trims, look for leaking injectors or high fuel pressure, check for exhaust leaks and test the oxygen sensors before replacing the catalytic converter.
